A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EigenBench and retain the same core research framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, allowing additions, replacements, and relocated material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original model rankings, persona experiments, model surveys, robustness tests, and judge-quality and confidence analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds human judgments, GPQA ranking experiments, character-training evaluation, constitution sensitivity tests, and a 37-model study.

M1.justification: The original judge scaffold, low-rank Bradley–Terry–Davidson model, and LM-only EigenTrust procedure remain. However, Appendix H adds joint human/LM judge modeling and hybrid aggregation through teleportation toward human trust vectors. Section 5.3 also introduces a constitution-free GPQA adaptation using answer-choice comparisons and ties for identical answers. These extend the procedure beyond simply evaluating the unchanged method on additional data.

E1.justification: v4 adds graduate-level scientific question answering through GPQA and a human-judgment study. Deep Ecology progresses from a documented constitution in v1 to reported evaluation in v4. The Claude-constitution/OpenAI-spec evaluation is replaced by evaluation using the Loving constitution. AskReddit, OpenAssistant, and AIRiskDilemmas remain in use.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained self-rating surveys, v4 adds human-derived scalar-BTD trust vectors as references for LM judgments and GPQA accuracy rankings as references for EigenBench rankings. These substantially broaden the comparison evidence. The scaffold-versus-no-scaffold comparator and its five judges are retained; additional evaluated LMs are not themselves new ranking-method baselines.

E3.justification: The main ranking experiment expands from five to eight models and from 24,000 to approximately 30,000 comparisons over 1,000 scenarios. Conservatism changes from eleven Gemini-assisted criteria to ten GPT-4.1-generated criteria. New designs include seven human judges, 448 GPQA questions, and a 37-model run with 140,000 comparisons over 2,000 scenarios. Character-training evaluation now compares base, prompted, and fine-tuned versions of the same Llama model.

E4.justification: v4 adds constitution-generation sensitivity testing and analyses of human judge embeddings and human-teleportation weights. It replaces the five-model confidence-width analysis with split-sample score stability on 37 models and replaces the 25-persona embedding-dimension experiment with a 37-model analysis. The original judge-quality and Greenbeard tests remain, with the latter moved to Appendix L.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix F uses 100 bootstrap resamples per confidence-interval estimate with adaptive repetitions. Its replacement in v4 Appendix K.1 uses 20 disjoint-subsample comparisons per sample size and reports Monte Carlo means and standard errors. GPQA validation adds a random-ranking probability calculation. The existing practice of displaying 95% percentile-bootstrap intervals for model rankings continues.

E6.justification: v4 replaces the main rankings and Claude/OpenAI-spec results and adds Loving scores of 1426, 1579, and 1573 for base, prompted, and fine-tuned Llama 3.1. New findings include human-human versus human-LM distances of 0.3133 versus 0.3130, GPQA Kendall tau approximately 0.77, and the 37-model leaderboard. Changed populations and constitutions prevent interpreting revised scores as same-setting gains. The 21%/79% variance decomposition, scenario-distribution scores, and judge-bias rates remain; the population-sensitivity table reorders existing values.

T1.justification: v4 adds formal definitions for human-guided teleportation and expected split-sample score instability, and changes the stated minimum model population from three to two. The original BTD likelihood, EigenTrust construction, and identifiability argument remain substantively unchanged. The variance decomposition is relocated to Appendix F, rather than newly derived.

C1.justification: v1's abstract emphasizes separating persona effects from persistent model dispositions. v4 instead foregrounds claims of agreement with human evaluators and recovery of objective GPQA rankings without labels. Its conclusion incorporates these validation claims into the justification for meaningful value rankings. The original disposition finding and proposed applications remain in the paper.

C2.justification: v4 qualifies the premise that models aligned with a trait are better judges of it, distinguishing kindness from plainspokenness. It adds interpretations of human agreement, constitution-wording robustness, and Deep Ecology's larger uncertainty from frequent ties. The dimension analysis now emphasizes the usefulness of larger embeddings for diverse populations. The conclusion newly discusses collection inefficiency and possible active-learning remedies; the Greenbeard limitation is retained.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-access link and explicit model identifiers for the main, GPQA, and 37-model experiments. It supplies the Loving criteria, revised constitution-generation information, and human-data collection details. The old Claude/OpenAI constitution lists disappear with their experiment. Adam settings and the generic persona and judge-scaffold prompts are retained. The PDFs establish the new access information, not whether the linked repository is operational.

R1.justification: v4 adds Maiya et al. on Open Character Training and Rein et al. on GPQA, while removing the Sharma et al. sycophancy reference. Existing Constitutional AI and deliberative-alignment discussion moves into related work. The principal positioning against LMArena, Prompt-to-Leaderboard, and LitmusValues remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are rewritten around validation, and the introduction expands its explanation of eigenvector weighting. Character-training background moves into related work; survey details, variance calculations, and Greenbeard analysis move into appendices. References and appendix organization are substantially reorganized. These changes alter the narrative structure beyond merely inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a single-column ICLR layout and redraws Figure 3 from two stacked horizontal-ranking panels into three side-by-side panels. It adds human-embedding, teleportation, and 37-model displays and restructures the stability/dimension plots. The causal data-collection diagram and separate tie-propensity heatmap are removed, while several retained figures and tables are relocated or reformatted.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens validation of what EigenBench scores measure. Human-judgment comparison, GPQA rank recovery, and the same-base-model character-training comparison address a central weakness of v1's predominantly internal evidence. Constitution sensitivity testing, larger-population analysis, and model identifiers further improve credibility and reproducibility. Some earlier diagnostics are removed, and the seven-person, single-constitution human study and extrapolation from GPQA still limit generalization. Nevertheless, the added validation provides a substantial overall quality gain.
